solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Landlord’s enduring delay losing current legal document (7,6)

indicatorNotes.losing: PATIENT loses the letter I, which stands for current

blocks.note: a landlord lets property, so is a LETTER; add the 'S
someone enduring a delay without fuss is patient
I is the symbol for electric current; it drops out of PATIENT to leave PATENT

annotation.surface: A landlord keeps putting off the paperwork, and the tenant waits for a legal document that never comes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Landlord' is not a synonym hunt for OWNER; read literally, a landlord is one who lets, a LETTER.
annotation.definitionFit: Letters patent are an open legal document issued by a monarch or government, granting a right, title or monopoly.

entries.clue: Vegetable, gas-friendly, needs cooking (5,6)

indicatorNotes.needs cooking: the letters of GAS-FRIENDLY are to be cooked, that is, mixed up

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A cook's note about a vegetable that won't give you wind, provided it is cooked.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that some vegetables are notoriously gassy; 'gas-friendly' is really just the letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Lady's finger is another name for okra, a green pod vegetable.

entries.clue: Foreign character’s ambassador in temperate area (5)

indicatorNotes.in: HE goes in between the two letters of TT

blocks.note: TT = teetotal, abstaining from drink
HE = His Excellency, an ambassador's title; it sits inside TT
A = area

annotation.surface: A foreign diplomat stationed somewhere with a mild climate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Temperate' suggests climate, but here it means sober: TT is the usual shorthand for teetotal.
annotation.definitionFit: Theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign character.

entries.clue: Keeping gun raised, erstwhile communist not inhibited (9)

indicatorNotes.Keeping: to keep something is to hold it, so TROT holds VER inside itself
indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raised means written bottom to top, so REV becomes VER

blocks.note: to gun an engine is to rev it
erstwhile = former, EX
TROT is short for Trotskyist; it holds VER

annotation.surface: A former communist who has put his gun away is no longer holding back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gun' looks like a weapon, but it is the verb, as in gunning an engine: REV.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym used adjectivally: an extrovert personality is outgoing, the opposite of shy and inhibited.

entries.clue: Perhaps Nemo’s position in minor title? (7)

blocks.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus, so he is the head of a sub
a lesser heading placed beneath a main one in a text

annotation.surface: Wondering where Captain Nemo ranks in some lesser title.
annotation.walkthrough: Captain Nemo is the submarine captain in Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas; 'Perhaps' flags him as one example of a sub's head.
annotation.definitionFit: A subhead is a secondary heading in a text, a minor title.

entries.clue: Completely skilled, fit guards extremely dependable (5)

indicatorNotes.guards: APT stands around DE, guarding it
indicatorNotes.extremely: take only the extreme letters of dependable

blocks.note: fit = suitable, apt
the first and last letters of DependablE, inside APT

annotation.surface: Praise for a worker: thoroughly skilled, fit, and dependable to the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guards' reads as a noun, soldiers, but it is the verb: APT stands around the two ends of dependable.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: adept means highly proficient, and 'Completely' stresses the degree.

entries.clue: Writer, unknown, tucks into succulent fruit on the turn (5,4)

indicatorNotes.tucks into: Z goes inside the reversed fruit
indicatorNotes.on the turn: ALOE LIME is turned round to read EMILEOLA

blocks.note: the aloe is a succulent plant
a lime is a fruit
z is an algebraic unknown, like x and y

annotation.surface: An unnamed writer tucks into a juicy fruit that is going off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Succulent fruit' reads as one juicy thing, but it is two: the plant ALOE and the fruit LIME.
annotation.definitionFit: Émile Zola was a French novelist, author of Germinal.

entries.clue: Digital process starts from theory of everything (3)

indicatorNotes.starts from: take the starting letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: first letters of Theory, Of, Everything

annotation.surface: Computing jargon: a digital process that starts from a grand unified theory of physics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Digital process' sounds like computing; a digit is also a finger or toe, and a process is an outgrowth of the body. Physicists do abbreviate the theory of everything as TOE.
annotation.definitionFit: A toe is one of the digits of the foot, a bodily process or projection.

entries.clue: Mistimed shot through slips … boundary! (4)

blocks.note: a cricket stroke where the ball glances off the side of the bat towards the slip fielders
a border or limit of something

annotation.surface: A cricket commentator's cry as a mishit flies past the slip fielders all the way to the boundary for four.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips are fielders standing beside the wicketkeeper, and the boundary is the rope round the field; here 'boundary' is just the plain word for a limit.
annotation.definitionFit: An edge is both a thin-bat cricket stroke and a boundary line.

entries.clue: Lentil and bean in mixture spilt over this? (5,5)

indicatorNotes.in mixture: LENTIL and BEAN are mixed together

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A lentil and bean stew slops over the tablecloth.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: what does a mixture of lentils and beans get spilt over at dinner?
annotation.definitionFit: Table linen, the tablecloth and napkins, is what food gets spilt on.

entries.clue: Look inside skip for thin meat slice (8)

indicatorNotes.inside: 'inside' means within, so the look word is placed within the skip word

blocks.note: to skip is to escape, as in skipping the country
lo! is an old word for look!

annotation.surface: A butcher is told to check inside a skip for some thin meat.
annotation.walkthrough: A skip is a British rubbish container, which makes the surface a bin search; here it is the verb meaning escape.
annotation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin slice of boneless meat, usually veal, beaten flat.

entries.clue: Channel swimmer crossing river (6)

indicatorNotes.crossing: TENCH lies across R, holding it inside

blocks.note: a tench is a freshwater fish, a swimmer
R = river

annotation.surface: A Channel swimmer crosses a river on the way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Channel swimmer' evokes the English Channel crossing, but 'Channel' alone is the definition and the swimmer is a fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch or channel.

entries.clue: Move a bar close to outdoor market (3,4,4)

indicatorNotes.Move: the letters of A BAR CLOSE TO are moved around

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone wants a pub moved nearer to the market.
annotation.walkthrough: A car boot sale is a British outdoor sale where people sell junk from the boots (trunks) of their cars, like a flea market.
annotation.definitionFit: A car boot sale is a kind of open-air market held in a field or car park.

entries.clue: Average sound reproduction perhaps with Bush player (10)

blocks.note: mid-fi sits between lo-fi and hi-fi, so middling sound reproduction
the elder is a bush

annotation.surface: A mediocre stereo paired with a Bush, a British brand of radio and TV sets.
annotation.walkthrough: Bush is a British electronics brand, which suits the hi-fi setting, but here it is a shrub. 'Perhaps' marks mid-fi as a coinage on the pattern of hi-fi.
annotation.definitionFit: A midfielder is a player in the middle of the field in football or hockey.

entries.clue: Stern woman honoured in amusing books (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the woman within the phrase that follows, so DAME sits between FUN and NT

blocks.note: amusing = fun
NT = New Testament, books of the Bible; FUN NT is the outer shell
a dame is a woman given a British honour, the female equivalent of a knighthood

annotation.surface: A severe woman is decorated for her funny books.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like an adjective (strict), but it is the noun: the rear end, of a ship or of a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Fundament is a formal word for the buttocks, the stern or backside.

entries.clue: Repeat fee after European bank’s set up (9)

indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so E TIER becomes REITE
indicatorNotes.after: RATE comes after the reversed piece

blocks.note: E = European
a bank is a row or tier, as a bank of seats
a fee or charge is a rate

annotation.surface: A European bank is being established and it charges a repeat fee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money beside 'fee', but it means a row, a tier.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to say or do something again, reiterate usually for emphasis.

entries.clue: Nasty person so backward (4)

indicatorNotes.backward: 'backward' means facing the wrong way, so the word for so is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so

annotation.surface: Calling someone nasty and a bit slow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backward' reads as dim-witted, which suits a nasty person; it only means reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative use: the man-eating giant of fairy tales lends his name to any cruel, frightening person.

entries.clue: Game introduced to an early Olympic Games? (4)

indicatorNotes.introduced to: to introduce something is to put it in, so the game is put into AN

blocks.note: Go is a Japanese board game
used as it stands, with GO inside

annotation.surface: A new game is introduced at one of the first Olympics.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: an agon was an athletic or artistic contest at the ancient Greek games, not the Olympics themselves.
annotation.definitionFit: Agon is ancient Greek for a contest, such as those held at the early Olympic Games.

entries.clue: One concluding art with no merit should be scrapped (10)

indicatorNotes.should be scrapped: the letters are scrapped and rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: ART and NO MERIT together give the ten letters to rearrange; 'with' just joins them

annotation.surface: An art critic's verdict: worthless work should be thrown out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One concluding' is a definition of the plain sort: a terminator is one who ends things.
annotation.definitionFit: A terminator is one who concludes or ends something.

entries.clue: Wrench has fixed two-wheeler (7)

indicatorNotes.fixed: HAS is fixed, rearranged, to give SHA

blocks.note: to rick a joint is to wrench or sprain it
HAS rearranged

annotation.surface: A mechanic takes a wrench to repair a bicycle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wrench' sounds like a spanner beside 'fixed', but it means a twist or sprain.
annotation.definitionFit: A ricksha, or rickshaw, is a light two-wheeled passenger cart pulled by a person.

entries.clue: Beat time welcoming Rugby School skipper (6)

blocks.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
RU = Rugby Union; it goes inside TAN
T = time

annotation.surface: The captain of Rugby School, a famous English boarding school, is welcomed at the right moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rugby School skipper' reads as the school captain, but the phrase splits: Rugby is RU and 'School skipper' is the definition, one who skips school.
annotation.definitionFit: A truant is a pupil who skips school without permission.

entries.clue: Article about Italian tax demanded by church (5)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so the article is placed around the Italian abbreviation

blocks.note: the definite article
IT = Italian; it sits inside THE

annotation.surface: A newspaper piece on an Italian levy imposed by the church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article THE.
annotation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of a person's produce or income, paid to support the church.

entries.clue: Preservative old drunkard consumed in endless crawl (8)

indicatorNotes.consumed in: O and SOT are swallowed by CREE

blocks.note: CREEP without its final P
O = old
a sot is a drunkard

annotation.surface: An old drunk, pickled from drinking, found on an endless pub crawl.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pub crawl, with the drunk 'preserved' in alcohol; the crawl is just CREEP.
annotation.definitionFit: Creosote is a tarry liquid used to preserve wooden fences and sheds.

entries.clue: Mystic Laplander drinking whiskey (5)

indicatorNotes.drinking: SAMI drinks W, taking it inside

blocks.note: the Sami are the native people of Lapland
Whiskey is the NATO alphabet word for W

annotation.surface: A Lapland shaman having a glass of whiskey.
annotation.walkthrough: Whiskey is not a drink here but the radio code word for W.
annotation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or holy man, a mystic.

entries.clue: Mean American holds leases in main region (7,3)

blocks.note: base = mean, low, ignoble
to lease is to rent; RENTS goes inside BASE
A = American

annotation.surface: A stingy American landlord holds leases on property in the principal region.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like chief, but it is the old poetic word for the sea, as in the Spanish Main; 'Mean' is not stingy but base.
annotation.definitionFit: The Barents Sea is a part of the Arctic Ocean north of Norway and Russia, a region of the main.

entries.clue: Turkish officer edges away from infidel (3)

indicatorNotes.edges away from: the edge letters of PAGAN are taken away

blocks.note: a pagan is an unbeliever; remove its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A Turkish officer edges away from an unbeliever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Edges away' reads as sidling off, but it means the edges, the outer letters, are taken away.
annotation.definitionFit: An aga was a military commander or official in the Ottoman Empire.

entries.clue: Architect, male linked with a Stateside lawyer … (4)

blocks.note: used as it stands
a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
M = male

annotation.surface: An architect teams up with an American lawyer, and the sentence runs on into the next clue.
annotation.walkthrough: Robert Adam was an 18th-century Scottish architect. The ellipsis joins this clue to 27 across for the surface only; each has its own answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Robert Adam was a famous Scottish neoclassical architect.

entries.clue: … still together (2,3,4,4)

blocks.note: still in the sense of nevertheless or even so
happening together, simultaneously

annotation.surface: Continuing 26: the architect and his lawyer partner are still together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as 'even now', but it is the other sense: nevertheless, however.
annotation.definitionFit: At the same time can mean both simultaneously and nevertheless.
